hints: State the head and tail probabilities for each coin: Coin 1 has P(H) = 1/4, P(T) = 3/4; Coins 2 and 3 each have P(H) = 1/2, P(T) = 1/2.
List all possible values of the number of heads X: x can be 0, 1, 2, or 3.
For P(X = 1), sum HTT (1/16), THT (3/16), and TTH (3/16) to get 7/16. For P(X = 2), sum HHT (1/16), HTH (1/16), and THH (3/16) to get 5/16. Verify that 3/16 + 7/16 + 5/16 + 1/16 = 1.
walkthrough:
Identify the independent probabilities for each coin:
$$\text{Coin 1: } \mathrm{P}(H) = \frac{1}{4}, \; \mathrm{P}(T) = \frac{3}{4}; \quad \text{Coins 2 and 3: } \mathrm{P}(H) = \frac{1}{2}, \; \mathrm{P}(T) = \frac{1}{2}$$

Calculate the probability for each outcome:
$$\mathrm{P}(X = 0) = \mathrm{P}(TTT) = \frac{3}{4} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{3}{16}$$
$$\mathrm{P}(X = 1) = \left(\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2}\right) + \left(\frac{3}{4} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2}\right) + \left(\frac{3}{4} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{1 + 3 + 3}{16} = \frac{7}{16}$$
$$\mathrm{P}(X = 2) = \left(\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2}\right) + \left(\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2}\right) + \left(\frac{3}{4} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{1 + 1 + 3}{16} = \frac{5}{16}$$
$$\mathrm{P}(X = 3) = \mathrm{P}(HHH) = \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{16}$$

Display the completed probability distribution table:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline x & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ \hline \mathrm{P}(X = x) & \frac{3}{16} & \frac{7}{16} & \frac{5}{16} & \frac{1}{16} \\ \hline \end{array}$$
$$\text{Check: } \frac{3}{16} + \frac{7}{16} + \frac{5}{16} + \frac{1}{16} = \frac{16}{16} = 1$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Understand the setup and list the individual probabilities:
Rachel throws three coins simultaneously:
- Coin 1 is biased: $\mathrm{P}(H_1) = \frac{1}{4}$, so $\mathrm{P}(T_1) = 1 - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{3}{4}$.
- Coin 2 is fair: $\mathrm{P}(H_2) = \frac{1}{2}$, so $\mathrm{P}(T_2) = \frac{1}{2}$.
- Coin 3 is fair: $\mathrm{P}(H_3) = \frac{1}{2}$, so $\mathrm{P}(T_3) = \frac{1}{2}$.
The random variable $X$ is the total number of heads obtained.

Step 2: Identify the set of possible values for $X$:
Since three coins are tossed, $X$ can take the values $0, 1, 2,$ or $3$.

Step 3: Calculate the probability of each value step-by-step:
- Case $X = 0$ (all three coins show tails):
$$\mathrm{P}(X = 0) = \mathrm{P}(T_1 \cap T_2 \cap T_3) = \frac{3}{4} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{3}{16} = 0.1875$$
- Case $X = 1$ (exactly one head):
Three mutually exclusive sequences yield one head:
  1. $H_1 T_2 T_3 \implies \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{16}$
  2. $T_1 H_2 T_3 \implies \frac{3}{4} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{3}{16}$
  3. $T_1 T_2 H_3 \implies \frac{3}{4} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{3}{16}$
Summing the three probabilities:
$$\mathrm{P}(X = 1) = \frac{1}{16} + \frac{3}{16} + \frac{3}{16} = \frac{7}{16} = 0.4375$$
- Case $X = 2$ (exactly two heads):
Three mutually exclusive sequences yield two heads:
  1. $H_1 H_2 T_3 \implies \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{16}$
  2. $H_1 T_2 H_3 \implies \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{16}$
  3. $T_1 H_2 H_3 \implies \frac{3}{4} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{3}{16}$
Summing the three probabilities:
$$\mathrm{P}(X = 2) = \frac{1}{16} + \frac{1}{16} + \frac{3}{16} = \frac{5}{16} = 0.3125$$
- Case $X = 3$ (all three coins show heads):
$$\mathrm{P}(X = 3) = \mathrm{P}(H_1 \cap H_2 \cap H_3) = \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{16} = 0.0625$$

Step 4: Check total probability sum:
$$\frac{3}{16} + \frac{7}{16} + \frac{5}{16} + \frac{1}{16} = \frac{16}{16} = 1$$
The sum is exactly 1, confirming the table is complete and valid.

Step 5: Present the probability distribution table clearly:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline x & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ \hline \mathrm{P}(X = x) & \frac{3}{16} & \frac{7}{16} & \frac{5}{16} & \frac{1}{16} \\ \hline \end{array}$$
